title: Transactional DB migrations and immutable release manifests for safer upgrades
author: Priya Bansal
commits: 3c9f2b1  chore(installer): introduce release manifest hashing and name-pinning
b7a4d8e  feat(migrations): implement transactional migration runner with advisory lock
d1f5a9c  feat(terraform): add pre-upgrade state snapshot helper and validate command
9a2e6b4  test: add e2e dry-run suite for upgrade path and rollback verification
f0b3c77  docs: add operational runbook for restore and post-upgrade checks
description:
Motivation: We observed two classes of upgrade failures in private deployments: partial schema application that left services mismatched, and Helm rollouts that could not be safely re-applied due to name collisions and mutable manifests. This PR introduces two complementary safety mechanisms: 1) a transactional DB migration runner that acquires an advisory lock, runs ordered up/down migrations in a single transaction where possible, and records a migration metadata file (migrations/META.json) pinned to the release SHA; and 2) immutable release manifests: Helm-generated manifests are now emitted to installer/manifests/<release-sha>/ and include content-hashed names for generated resources (ConfigMaps/Jobs) so that reapplying a previous release is idempotent and tombstone-friendly.

What changed (high-level):
- New migration runner (installer/migrations/runner.go and bin/rwi-migrate): supports --dry-run, --apply, --rollback <target>, --advisory-lock and writes a migrations/META.json with {release_sha, applied_at, migrations}. The runner falls back to safe single-statement execution when DB does not support transactional DDL (we detect via feature probe).
- Helm pipeline change: chart packaging now includes a pre-render step that materializes manifests to installer/manifests/{{release_sha}}/ and substitutes stable, immutable names for ConfigMaps and Jobs (e.g. config-{{sha}}). This avoids name reuse and makes rollbacks predictable.
- Terraform helper: scripts/terraform-snapshot.sh takes a consistent remote state snapshot and uploads to the cluster backup bucket before performing an upgrade. The installer will refuse to proceed if a snapshot is not available unless --force is passed.
- Restore tooling: bin/rwi-rollback.sh coordinates restoring TF state, reapplying the previous manifest set, and invoking rwi-migrate --rollback <previous-sha>. A minimal operator-level health check ensures that KV caches are cleared before accepting traffic.
- Tests and CI: Added an e2e dry-run pipeline that runs the migration runner against a test Postgres instance, performs a simulated upgrade by rendering manifests to tmp/<sha>, and verifies that rollback brings the cluster back to the previous schema and resource set.

Design notes:
- We adopted metadata-versioning: every release has a release SHA that is propagated into migrations/META.json and into rendered manifest paths. This makes state and migrations addressable by release identity and avoids implicit "latest" assumptions.
- Transactionality: where the DB supports transactional DDL (Postgres 12+ with standard behavior), we wrap multiple migration files in a single transaction and only record META.json after commit. When not supported, we run each migration guarded with idempotency checks and emit detailed logs so operators can inspect partially-applied steps.
- Downgrade guard: the runner enforces a policy (configurable) that prevents auto-downgrade of certain immutable schema changes unless an explicit --allow-downgrade flag is provided and a validated snapshot exists.
- Operational ergonomics: added rwi backup/restore subcommands and an Ops runbook (docs/ops/upgrade-and-rollback.md) that contains step-by-step commands, expected durations, and troubleshooting guidance.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge and ship to canary clusters with feature-flag enabled.
2) Run an automated canary upgrade with full snapshot + dry-run.
3) Collect metrics (upgrade duration, migration runtime, failures) and iterate.
4) Gate enabling for customer upgrades behind a documented checklist.

References: ENG-4823, PM-177, SUP-2145.

Author (Priya): Added signal handling and a graceful shutdown path that releases the advisory lock and writes a partial-state artifact. See runner.go:handleSignals (comment added).
Lina Chen: Helm pre-render changes look good; please ensure we preserve release notes and CRD ordering when materializing manifests. (approved)

merge_details: Merged via squash on 2026-02-22 by Priya Bansal. Commit message summarises the transactional migrations, immutable manifests, and restore tooling. Merge method: squash/merge.
release_notes: Private installer: safer upgrades — transactional DB migration runner (with advisory-locks and dry-run), immutable release manifests materialized to per-release folders, pre-upgrade Terraform state snapshots, and an automated rollback helper script. Operators must run 'scripts/terraform-snapshot.sh' before scheduled upgrades. See docs/ops/upgrade-and-rollback.md for full runbook.
operational_runbook: Rollback: ./bin/rwi-rollback.sh --from-sha=<previous-sha> (this will restore TF state, reapply manifests, and invoke migrations --rollback)
Post-upgrade checks: prometheus SLOs, migration logs, and operator health checks (see docs/ops/upgrade-and-rollback.md)
